clue.text: Pick head off flower in daring fashion

parts.note: to pick a string or a flower is to pluck it

indicators.note: taking the head off a word drops its first letter, here from the flower's name

parts.note: a lily is a flower

explanation.surface: Someone boldly snaps the head off a flower they have picked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' tempts you to look for a bloom as the answer, but it is fodder; 'head off' beheads it, and the definition is the adverbial phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting pluckily means acting with courage, which is doing things in a daring fashion.

clue.text: Quiet cat's bound to catch prey

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
the ounce, or snow leopard, is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A silent cat is sure to catch its victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain', but it is the noun for a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pounce is a sudden leap or spring made to seize a victim.

clue.text: Like CID but not the police, in drug investigation

definitions.text: Like CID but not the police

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
a case is a matter investigated by detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives, not uniformed police, look into narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department; 'but not the police' tells you to read CID simply as three capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are called upper-case, from the printer's case holding them; CID is written that way.

clue.text: Shrewd ruler concealing present

indicators.note: concealing means the word for ruler hides the word for present inside it

parts.note: a king is a ruler
now means the present time

explanation.surface: A clever monarch hides a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' suggests a gift, but here it means the present moment; 'concealing' tells you the ruler holds it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing means shrewd, astute, showing awareness.

clue.text: Game played by gamblers and by fool

parts.note: loo is an old card game played for stakes

explanation.surface: Gamblers and a fool play at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A looby is an old word for a clumsy, stupid person, a lout or simpleton.

clue.text: Sweetheart I love returned drill

indicators.note: returned means the whole run of sweetheart, I and love is read backwards

parts.note: a sweetheart is a girl
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lover's message about going back to some routine practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns GIRL + I + O round as one string, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshore rig is the structure that drills for petroleum, so it is a drill in the noun sense.

clue.text: With diamonds to carry, it helps to keep a cool head

definitions.text: it helps to keep a cool head

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
to pack is to carry, as in packing a gun

explanation.surface: A jewel courier is told to stay calm under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep a cool head' sounds like staying calm, but it is literal: a cold compress.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of crushed ice pressed on the brow chills it, a remedy for a fever or bump.

clue.text: Almost finished dressing bird

indicators.note: almost finished means the word is not quite completed, losing its final letter

parts.note: robing is dressing in robes

explanation.surface: Someone has nearly dressed a bird for cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost finished' drops the G from ROBING.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a common garden songbird with a red breast.

clue.text: Like charity, above all

explanation.surface: Charity is praised above everything.
explanation.walkthrough: From 1 Corinthians 13: 'faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.'
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul names charity the top virtue of the three; anything supreme over all others is the best, the highest.

clue.text: Novelist has to omit 21

parts.note: C.P. Snow was an English novelist
to drop is to omit or leave out

explanation.surface: A writer is told to cut something out.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is BLOOMER, here in its sense of something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowdrop is an early spring flower, so it is a bloomer.

clue.text: Powerless to include part of speech church makes impossible to deliver

indicators.note: to include means the word for powerless takes the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: powerless means unable
a pronoun is one of the parts of speech in grammar
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A weak preacher finds a passage of the church service too hard to read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' splits the word for powerless around the grammar term and the church abbreviation; 'deliver' means say aloud, as delivering a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A word too awkward to say cannot be delivered in speech: a sense of uttering, pronouncing.

clue.text: It can be taken out of concert if you provide written confirmation

indicators.note: can be taken out of signals a run of letters lifted straight from the words concert if you

explanation.surface: A music fan learns what may be removed from a concert if they put it in writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'conCERT IF You'.
explanation.definitionFit: To certify is to attest formally, typically in a signed document.

clue.text: Undistinguished object used as furniture

explanation.surface: An ordinary item pressed into service as furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a thing not worth naming, a vague object; it is also a stand of open shelves for ornaments, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Beetle's survival

explanation.surface: An insect lives on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' is the verb meaning to overhang, as beetling brows jut out; the insect is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle is to project or jut over; a relic left from an earlier time is a survival, also called a holdover.

clue.text: The carriage is in the station

explanation.surface: A coach stands at a railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: London Victoria is a major railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A victoria is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage; Victoria is also a London rail terminus.

clue.text: Draper's assistant is sleeping soundly

indicators.note: soundly here signals a word that is heard rather than seen, not deep slumber

parts.note: kips is British slang for sleeps

explanation.surface: The shop assistant has nodded off deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Kipps, hero of H.G. Wells's novel 'Kipps', is a draper's apprentice in Folkestone.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the Wells novel is apprenticed to a draper, a dealer in cloth.

clue.text: It's very close to defeat for the team at the top

indicators.note: at the top means the pieces for the team and for are placed above, before the word for defeat

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team
mate is checkmate, defeat in chess

explanation.surface: The leading side came near to losing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'at the top' means placed above, so 'for' and 'the team' come first; 'very close' is the definition despite sitting mid-clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means nearest, immediately next, in close proximity.

clue.text: Person who's tried embracing queen is doomed

indicators.note: embracing means the defendant's word wraps round the letter for queen

parts.note: the accused is the person on trial
R is regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A defendant who hugs the monarch is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' wraps the defendant round the queen's letter; 'tried' is the law-court sense, not attempted.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means under a curse, ill-fated.

clue.text: Pleasant voyage announced for sailors here

indicators.note: announced signals that the phrase for a pleasant voyage is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a cruise is a pleasure trip by sea

explanation.surface: A holiday sea trip is advertised to seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' just points to where the sailors are, the crews of the ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's crew is its body of seamen, so crews are groups of sailors.

clue.text: Dog losing tail in trap

indicators.note: losing tail means the dog's name drops its last letter

parts.note: a springer is a spaniel breed

explanation.surface: A dog has its tail caught in a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tail' removes the final R of SPRINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A springe is a snare for small game, a noose set on a bent stick.

clue.text: Imitate publication (not novel)

parts.note: to imitate is to copy
a book is a publication

explanation.surface: Someone copies a published work that is not a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not novel)' looks like an aside about the book, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Copybook as an adjective means conventional and exactly by the rules, hence unoriginal.

clue.text: Mistake made by American social reformer

explanation.surface: An error is blamed on a US campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: Amelia Bloomer was a nineteenth-century American campaigner for women's rights and dress reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder; Amelia Bloomer promoted the loose trousers named after her.

clue.text: Got better as symptom finally stopped appearing

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of symptom is used

parts.note: ended means stopped

explanation.surface: A patient recovered as the signs of illness went away.
explanation.definitionFit: To have mended is to have healed or recovered, as a broken bone does.

clue.text: Suffer, being less than fit

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten
go means fit and working, as in all systems go

explanation.surface: Someone out of condition puts up with hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo is to experience or endure something unpleasant.

clue.text: Folding seat is unsteady

explanation.surface: A fold-out seat wobbles.
explanation.walkthrough: A dicky seat is a folding seat in the back of an old car; dicky is British for weak or shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dicky is a fold-down rear seat in old cars; dicky also means shaky or unreliable, as in a dicky heart.

clue.text: Sweet food that's excellent, and cold inside

indicators.note: inside means the letter for cold goes within the word for excellent

parts.note: choice means excellent, of top quality
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A dessert described as superb and chilled within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places the cold abbreviation within the word for excellent. A choc ice is a British block of ice cream coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: A choc ice is a chocolate-coated ice-cream bar, a confection or sweet treat.

clue.text: Store to get ready for, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for getting ready money is spoken, giving one that sounds alike

parts.note: to cash a cheque is to get ready money, cash in hand, for it

explanation.surface: A shop promises to prepare for something, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for cash money; 'to get ready for' a cheque is to cash it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden hoard, a store of supplies or valuables.

clue.text: Vice-captain, perhaps? In MCC. one's odd man out

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A deputy captain is the misfit at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: The MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club, which runs Lord's cricket ground in London; the cricket is a disguise, as the letters of IN MCC ONES ODD MAN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy leader ranks just below the chief; a vice-captain is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Poet it's not interesting to study

parts.note: dry means dull, not interesting
a den is a room for quiet work, a study

explanation.surface: A student complains a poet is boring to read.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a seventeenth-century English poet laureate.

clue.text: Develop affection for, have brief entanglement, then stop

indicators.note: entanglement means the word brief is tangled up, its letters rearranged

parts.note: to end is to stop

explanation.surface: A short-lived romance that is then broken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entanglement' scrambles the word brief, giving BEFRI; 'brief entanglement' looks like a fling, which suits the definition's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To befriend someone is to make a friend of them, growing fond of them.
